Overview
The task is to provide a manufacturing ready lipo/li-ion battery charger PCB using npm1100 PMIC.
Objectives
Project objectives
Reading the datasheet and finding the basic outline of the IC and how it is to be configured.
Design a schematic based on the information provided in the datasheet and then make a basic PCB with the required specifications.
Perform the Design Rule Check and Electrical Rule Check.
Documentation
Analysing the datasheet for key points and example circuits
Source: Datasheet
Block Diagram![](data:image/png;base64,)
The above given diagram shows the internal of the ic and the pinouts of the IC.
We move on to what are the pins and their functions
VBUS, D+, D-, ISET: These pins provide a bus for the USB interface with the IC.
VBAT, AVSS, NTC: These pins work their way to the battery. The VBAT and the AVSS pin will charge the battery whereas the NTC pin will help in communication with the battery to keep track of the battery temperature.
VTERMSET: This pin helps in communicating with the IC for the battery charging voltage.
![](data:image/png;base64,)
ICHG: This pin sets the current for charging the battery and sets the current based on the formula![](data:image/png;base64,)
SHPACT,SHPHLD: These pins are used to communicate with the IC if the ship mode is Active.
VSYS: It provides a stable output voltage to power devices like a MCU.
DEC: It has to be connected to a decoupling capacitor to stable/smooth the internal voltage.
SW, VOUTB: The SW node is used to toggle between HIGH and LOW in the VOUTB and smooth the output which is buck buck output.
VOUTBSET1, VOUTBSET2: The battery output voltage can be set to a value using these pins according to the below given diagram.![](data:image/png;base64,)
MODE: The MODE pin configures the PMIC operation mode.
CHG,ERR: These pins are used to get the charging status and error indication.

PCB Design
Now we can update the schematics in the pcb editor. As we get the required components and traces. We define a 35 mm x 35 mm edgecut rectangle for a tentative limit for the space.  
We can now place the required footprints and then route the trace neatly using via’s to communicate between the 2 layers(Front and Back).  
We make sure the DRC is running simultaneously and edit the trace width and minimum trace separation according to the manufacturing rules.  
![](data:image/png;base64,)  
Finally we reduce the size of the pcb by reducing the edgecut layer rectangle.  
We also make drill holes in the remaining place for functionality.
